learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the nuanced structures of English tenses, specifically focusing on the Perfect and Perfect Continuous forms, and understand when to use them contextually.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 We already know the basics of Past, Present, and Future. But time isn't just a simple straight line! Sometimes actions are ongoing, and sometimes they started in the past but are still affecting us right now. Let's master the advanced forms of time travel!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Continuous tenses show that an action is, was, or will be happening over a period of time. They are formed using 'to be' verbs (is/are/was/were/will be) + the present participle (verb + -ing).
examples_or_templates: Present Continuous: I **am studying** for my exams.
Past Continuous: They **were playing** when the rain started.
Future Continuous: She **will be sleeping** at 10 PM.

lesson_modules.module_title: ✅ The Perfect Tenses: The 'Completed' Actions (पूर्ण काल)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Perfect tenses tell us about actions that are completely finished by a certain point in time. They are formed using 'have/has/had/will have' + the past participle (3rd form of the verb).
examples_or_templates: Present Perfect: I **have finished** my homework. (Finished recently, affects now)
Past Perfect: The train **had left** before we reached the station. (Two past actions, one happened first)

lesson_modules.module_title: ⏳ Perfect Continuous: The 'Marathon' Tenses (पूर्ण निरंतर काल)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: These tenses talk about an action that started in the past and has been going on continuously up to another point. They combine the rules: have/has/had + been + verb + -ing. We often use 'since' or 'for' with them.
examples_or_templates: Present Perfect Continuous: It **has been raining** since morning.
Past Perfect Continuous: He **had been driving** for five hours when the car broke down.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the tense: 'I have been living in this city for ten years.'
❓ Choose the correct verb form for the Past Perfect tense: 'She realized she _____ her keys at home.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this sentence to the Future Continuous tense: 'They play cricket.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use 'will be' + the 'ing' form of the verb.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank using the Present Perfect tense: 'My brother _____ (eat) all the cookies!'
subjective_practice.hint: Use 'has' because 'brother' is singular, and the 3rd form of 'eat'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Combine these two past actions using the Past Perfect tense: 'The movie started. Then we arrived at the cinema.'
subjective_practice.hint: Which action happened first? Give it the 'had + V3' treatment: 'The movie had... before we...'

activity_or_assignment.title: 🕰️ The Personal Timeline
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write three true sentences about your life. One in Present Perfect (something you have achieved), one in Present Continuous (something you are currently doing these days), and one in Present Perfect Continuous (a hobby you have been doing for a long time)!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Continuous tenses (be + V-ing) show ongoing actions at a specific time.
⭐ Perfect tenses (have/has/had + V3) show actions completed before a certain point in time.
⭐ Perfect Continuous tenses (have/has/had + been + V-ing) emphasize how long an ongoing action has been happening.
